accepted.question_text: For an arbitrary diversity (X, δ) on n points, what is the smallest worst-case function f(n) such that every such diversity admits an embedding into some ℓ1 diversity (R^d, δ̂) with distortion at most f(n)? Equivalently, determine the optimal asymptotic upper bound for the minimal distortion required to embed any n-point diversity into ℓ1 when the target dimension d is unrestricted.

evidence.quote: Problem: Find a bound f (n) such that for any diversity (X , δ ) with |X | = n there is a map φ from (X , δ ) into an ℓ1 diversity (Rd , δ̂ ) with distortion at most f (n).
As we explain below, the best general bound we have so far is O(n), though this is likely far from optimal. We know that the bound cannot be better than Ω(log n).

accepted.question_text: Can one design a hybrid embedding method for diversities that combines the advantages of Bourgain-style arguments, which give low-distortion embeddings for diameter diversities, with Bartal-style tree-based arguments, which work for Steiner diversities, in order to obtain stronger general ℓ1 distortion bounds for arbitrary diversities? In particular, is there a principled way to use a Bartal-type approach on parts of the problem while switching to a Bourgain-type approach on subproblems where tree methods fail?

evidence.quote: We have shown that Bourgain’s approach embeds δdiam with small distortion, but applying the metric result directly does appear to give an embedding for δS . On the other hand, Bartal’s approach embeds δS , but does not successfully embed all diameter diversities. Is some hybrid approach possible, perhaps one which applies Bartal’s approach but switches to a Bourgain approach for some subproblems?

accepted.question_text: Can expander-hypergraph methods be developed to prove nontrivial lower bounds on the distortion needed to embed diversities into ℓ1, analogous to the role that expander graphs play for metric embeddings into ℓ1? More specifically, can the connection between diversity embedding and hypergraph sparsest cut be turned into rigorous lower-bound constructions for diversity distortion?

evidence.quote: Expander graphs have proven to be a good source for lower bounds on the distortion required to embed metrics in ℓ1 . Expander hypergraphs are far less understood, but perhaps analogous arguments could be used to obtain lower bounds on the distortion of diversities, particularly given the connections between diversity embedding and hypergraph sparsest cut established in [5].

accepted.question_text: Does every n-point diversity admit an ℓ1 embedding with distortion O(sqrt(n)) by a construction that depends only on the induced metric d(x, y) = δ({x, y}) and not on any additional diversity-specific information? Equivalently, is there an embedding procedure derived solely from the induced metric that matches the known barrier that no such metric-only method can do better than Ω(sqrt(n)) in general?

evidence.quote: We know that we cannot obtain a distortion bound in this way that is better than Ω(√n), as we showed in Part 2 of our discussion of Bourgain’s approach. We conjecture that there exists an embedding based solely on the induced metric which nevertheless achieves an O(√n) distortion bound for all diversities.
